articles.title_orig: ‘Forever cruise’ ship Odyssey impounded in Singapore, records show
articles.title_zh: ‘Forever cruise’ ship Odyssey impounded in Singapore, records show
articles.content_orig:
The Odyssey, the "forever cruise" left stranded in Southeast Asia after its owner struggled with financial problems , has been held by authorities in Singapore, according to court records obtained by CBS News.
A Singaporean law firm, Helmsman LLC, is listed as the solicitor in the "arrest" of the ship, but it is unclear whom the firm is representing. A source familiar with the matter told CBS News it is likely a fuel supplier.
"The vessel has been placed under arrest pursuant to a court order," Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority said in a statement cited by the French news agency AFP and other outlets on Monday. "The crew onboard are reported to be well, and arrangements for their welfare and wellbeing are being managed by the vessel's creditors. There are no passengers on board."
It added that the ship was "anchored in Singapore port waters." AFP described the ship as being "impounded" by Singaporean authorities.
The luxury cruise ship is currently being operated by its lender after its owner, Villa Vie Residences, couldn't keep up with payments.
Villa Vie owes one supplier in the area approximately $500,000, though it's unclear whether that supplier hired the law firm to solicit the arrest.
A ship arrest is a legal process in Singapore in which a vessel can be detained or seized following a legal claim.
The journey of the MV Odyssey luxury cruise ship, launched in October 2024, came to a sudden end last month in Cambodia, where residents on the ship had just hours to disembark.
According to accounts from multiple sources familiar with the final weeks on board, these details included a scramble to find fuel while stuck at a port in Singapore, a rush by the crew to obtain provisions once food shipments had ended, and the temporary detainment of the ship in Hong Kong.
AFP cited Villa Vie Residences as saying "extraordinary increases" in the cost of fuel amid the U.S. war with Iran had driven its monthly fuel expenses from about $1,800 per guest cabin, to as much as $8,000 in some parts of Asia, where many nations rely heavily on imports from the Persian Gulf.
This story published first on CBS News at 6:24 p.m. on Nov. 8, 2026.

articles.title_orig: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
articles.title_zh: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
articles.content_orig:
The perfect nightmare scenario for a Linux server is when all an attacker needs to do is reach the server’s Secure Shell (SSH) port, waltz right in, and take it over. That’s what happened to Alpine Linux , the popular, lightweight Linux server. Adding insult to injury, this happened only days after Alpine Linux dodged a security hole-sized bullet to its GitLab implementation.
Also: Linux Mint 27 arrives next month, and I like it already: What to expect
How bad is it? As bad as it can get. Alpine Linux explained in its security advisory that if an attacker can reach a vulnerable server’s SSH port, they can get in “with one connection,” and the attack “works every time, and needs no retries.”
As security engineer Gregory Bryant explained in his LinkedIn post :
Most authentication bypasses come from complex logic chains, but yesterday’s Alpine Linux OpenSSH vulnerability ( CVE-2026-123158 ) comes down to a single character: *.”
If you run Alpine Linux (or another musl-based distro) with the default openssh-server package (no Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) ) and PasswordAuthentication enabled, an attacker can log into password-disabled, or key-only accounts simply by sending a password between 257 and 1024 bytes long.
Alpine Linux isn’t the only operating system that uses musl , a lightweight version of the standard C library (libc). Other operating systems that use musl and are potentially vulnerable include Adélie Linux; Void Linux; Sabotage Linux; OpenWrt, an Android variant,  and the Yocto Project, which is used to build embedded Linux distributions.
Also: This clever banking scam keeps phishing by faking its own demise
Wind River, which produces the commercial embedded Linux distro, Wind River Linux, is also looking into the issue. A company representative told me, “Wind River takes security seriously. We are actively reviewing the reported vulnerability and assessing its potential impact. We will take appropriate action as needed.”
Behind the scenes, when OpenSSH is built without PAM, it verifies passwords by hashing the password attempt using the C library’s crypt() function. It then compares the result to the account’s stored password field. So far, so good.
But when a key is longer than 256 bytes, musl’s crypt() function returns the string * as an error indicator. That is also what the password field holds for any account with no password, such as a key-only account. Thus, the “hash” matches and the login succeeds, and the attacker walks in.
Also: The new Cutefish Linux distro might be the best MacOS clone around
To exploit it, an attacker only needs the name of such an account. The attacker also needs at least one other account on the machine with a 5 or 6 password hash, and then to send a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes. According to Alpine, one user with a password is enough to make every passwordless account accessible.
In Linux systems that use glibc’s crypt(), which is almost all of them, the same attempt would return NULL on error, which sshd already rejects, so Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, etc., aren’t affected.
According to *sshole , the group that uncovered the problem, this is a side effect that has been hiding since 2016.
Alpine said every release it checked is affected: 3.21 through 3.24, edge, and the older 3.16 to 3.20 branches. Exposure requires the following:
Root is not directly exposed in most cases. It has shipped as root:* in the base image since about Alpine 3.16, but OpenSSH’s default PermitRootLogin prohibit-password blocks it. Another account that can become root, for example through doas, still gives an attacker a route to root.
Alpine singled out its official tiny-cloud images, versions 3.18.11 through 3.24.3, as especially vulnerable. These ship with an alpine user with a * password field and passwordless doas. They are safe on first boot but become exploitable once any 6 hash exists on the machine. That can happen when an administrator sets a console password or when user data adds a user with a hashed password, which means, essentially, all of them.
Alpine said these are not affected:
Alpine released 3.21.10, 3.22.8, 3.23.8 and 3.24.4 on Thursday, with the OpenSSH fix among the security changes. It also published fixed packages for each release back to 3.16. Alpine 3.21 reached end of support on Nov. 1.
The just-released OpenSSH 10.6p2 avoids the problem in sshd. Alpine’s stable branches carry a patch for the same problem. You should run apk upgrade -U -a and then restart the daemon with rc-service sshd restart. Alpine stressed that upgrading the package does not replace the running daemon. Anyone who cannot update should set PasswordAuthentication no and restart sshd, after confirming that key login works.
Also: Maze Linux is the best security-focused distro I’ve ever tested
To check for an attack, Alpine told administrators to search /var/log/messages for “Accepted password for” lines that name an account with no password. It also advised reviewing dedicated OpenBSD application subexecutor (doas) use and recently created users, files, and authorized keys. “If you cannot rule out a login, treat the machine as compromised.” Just what you wanted for your weekend, I know, but here we are.

articles.title_orig: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
articles.title_zh: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic on Monday released two new artificial intelligence models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the company readies for a potentially historic IPO that could take place as soon as next week.
Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are Anthropic's most advanced offerings, and the company said they generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors. The models also cost 20% less than the 5.1 generation, and will be available for $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, the company said.
The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released so-called "frontier" models since its CEO, Dario Amodei , called to slow down the pace of AI development in September . Anthropic said the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.
"We called for pacing, not pausing," Dianne Penn, Anthropic's head of product management for research, told CNBC in an interview.
Anthropic has to balance its safety efforts with intense commercial and competitive pressures, a tension that the company highlighted in the extensive risk factors section of its prospectus late last month. And as executives prepare to kick off Anthropic's IPO roadshow , they'll have to convince investors that their approach is the right one.
The company is aiming for a valuation of $1 trillion to $1.5 trillion in its offering, as CNBC previously reported , down from a target of $2 trillion that had been floated in recent months.
Anthropic first introduced Mythos in April, and it limited the rollout to a select group of organizations because of the model's advanced cybersecurity capabilities. The company introduced Fable , a publicly available version of Mythos with additional safeguards, two months later.
The models — particularly Mythos — captivated Wall Street and government officials alike, and they helped to fuel Anthropic's meteoric rise this year. The company said in its amended prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year.
Penn said Fable 5.2 is primarily intended for "power users or power use cases" since it excels at complex, open-ended technical work. Other models like Claude Opus 5.5 , which Anthropic released in September, are better suited for daily tasks, so Penn said users should turn to Fable 5.2 when they need to tackle hard problems in engineering, mathematics and robotics.
"These are just net new things that are completely novel, and so they're frontier use cases," Penn said. "We expect that over time to maybe trickle to the Opus class, but really right now we do see a difference in terms of performance that we think those frontier use cases benefit from."
Anthropic said Fable 5.2 is generally available on Monday, and Mythos 5.2 is available to vetted organizations through the company's Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.

articles.title_zh: Not Revenue. Not Growth. Here’s What I’ll Be Watching When CoreWeave and Nebius Report This Week.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
It's been a rough few weeks to own CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) or Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS). Both stocks have lost close to half their value since early October. Both companies report earnings this week -- CoreWeave on Tuesday, followed by Nebius on Thursday -- that may have serious consequences for shareholders.
Here's what to know ahead of these critical releases.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
While the stocks have been sliding for some time, last Tuesday's sweeping Democratic midterm victory led to a roughly 14% drop in less than a week as investors weighed what the results would mean for the AI build-out.
Democratic candidates across the country ran on platforms that promised to rein in data center building and increase oversight of the AI industry at large. It worked. The topic became a flashpoint and helped propel Democrats to victory in states where the build-out is in full swing.
Data center moratoriums were central campaign pitches for the governors-elect in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia -- key states in the AI buildout.
CoreWeave has six active sites in Texas. Nebius faces its own challenges in states like Pennsylvania, which has already tightened its permitting rules and has a full moratorium under consideration.
The election results were hardly the start of the companies' recent woes. They've just amplified concerns over the sustainability of their business models -- especially given CoreWeave's heavy reliance on debt financing.
This is an expensive business. Without the resources of the big tech hyperscalers like Meta (NASDAQ:META) or Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), CoreWeave has been forced to take on serious debt to fund its growth. The company currently carries $35.1 billion in on-the-books debt.
Concerns around the company's borrowing led the yield on some of CoreWeave's bonds above 16% as of last week. At the same time, the cost to insure those bonds against default skyrocketed.
Nebius, on the other hand, relies less on financing, carrying $8.5 billion. However, that could change. The company lined up a $3.5 billion loan facility from Citi in October, and Reuters reported that it was considering a high-yield bond sale, but ultimately passed.
And that was before the added risk of a data center construction slowdown.
Wall Street is expecting another big quarter from both companies. Analysts are looking for:
CoreWeave: $3.55 billion in sales, or about 160% growth
Nebius: $908 million, or about 500% growth
These are obviously extreme growth rates that any company would envy. I think both companies will have to overperform these targets while also showing costs are improving as a bare minimum.
Image source: Getty Images.
But I'll be paying more attention to what management says about construction and borrowing costs. What impacts will the election results have on the already planned projects? If any delays are expected, how will that impact cash flows? What is CoreWeave's plan if borrowing costs keep rising? Can it afford to borrow at 16% interest, and for how long?
And for Nebius, does its recent $3.5 billion credit facility signal it will need to rely more on borrowing than it has in the past? How will this impact its cash flows?

articles.title_orig: Minnesota candy store owner charged over liquor-filled candy
articles.title_zh: Minnesota candy store owner charged over liquor-filled candy
articles.content_orig:
The owner of Minnesota's Largest Candy Store in Jordan is facing a gross misdemeanor count of selling an alcoholic product without a license after an anonymous tipster alleged a child was sold liquor-filled candies this summer without an ID check.
According to court documents filed last month in Scott County, the tip was sent to the Minnesota Department of Public Safety's Alcohol and Gambling Enforcement Division on July 1.
Later that month, agents with the department visited the store and found "a section dedicated to alcoholic beverage candies and confections," including Asbach Pralinen Brandy Cherries, according to the criminal complaint, with a alcohol concentration 7.3%, and a Goldkenn Jack Daniel's Tennessee Fire Swiss chocolate liqueur, with a 3.58% concentration.
The complaint states the agents observed warnings on the back of the products that state they can't be sold to minors, but "the items did not have a separate procedure compared to non-alcohol filled items."
Investigators allege when agents confronted the store's owner, 66-year-old Robert Mark Wagner, he confirmed he didn't have a liquor license, according to court documents, and was under the impression he "could sell all the alcoholic confections and beverage candies" he had in stock.
Wagner, of Belle Plaine, Minnesota, was not arrested. He's set to make his first court appearance on Dec. 18.
The charge against Wagner carries a maximum of a year in jail and a $3,000 fine, according to the county attorney's office.

articles.content_orig:
Logic Pro is Apple’s first app to charge for extended usage of Apple Intelligence.﻿
Logic Pro is Apple’s first app to charge for extended usage of Apple Intelligence.﻿
After publishing a support article in early September outlining usage limits for some Apple Intelligence features, the company has updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for a one-time purchase price of $49.99, as spotted by 9to5Mac . It has a built-in AI assistant to do things like “start a new song, set up a vocal track from a single prompt, or refine an active project.”
These Intelligence Usage Packs, as Apple calls them, will allow users to continue accessing certain Apple Intelligence features that have usage limits because they rely on cloud-based AI models from OpenAI or Google Gemini. The Usage Packs can only be used by the Apple Account that purchased them (Family Sharing isn’t supported) and, as Apple explains on its website , any unused additional usage will roll over from month to month, but will expire 12 months after it was purchased.
For Logic Pro, Apple says the usage limit is “impacted by the complexity of conversations you have with the assistant.” Users finding themselves running out of access can find the option to buy an Intelligence Usage Pack in the Intelligence Features > Show Usage section of the app’s main menu. Currently, only Logic Pro has the option to buy more usage, but it’s expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers that are getting access to Apple’s AI chatbot .

articles.title_orig: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges
articles.title_zh: France, U.S. Suspect Iran Was Behind Cyberattack on European Fridges
articles.content_orig:
France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.
Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions.
Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.
The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.
Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".
He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".
France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.
The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.
Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.
Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.
In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.
If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy.
On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.
More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.
Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.
In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.
The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.
Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian.

articles.title_zh: China’s rare-earth rubber trades at 22,500 yuan a tonne, about 35% above standard rubber
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
China is testing whether a premium rubber can win a place in electric-vehicle tires. Rare-earth cis-butadiene rubber, made with a rare-earth catalyst, now has a Xinjiang plant rated at 100,000 metric tons a year, about 110,000 U.S. tons. It also trades at a higher price than conventional synthetic rubber.
China Rubber Industry Association data published Nov. 2 quoted rare-earth grade ND9106 at 22,500 yuan (about US$3,400) per metric ton during Oct. 26 to Nov. 1. Conventional BR9000 in Shandong province was quoted at 16,660 yuan per metric ton, so the rare-earth grade carried a premium of about 35%.
For tire makers, the rubber offers better wear resistance, greater strength and lower rolling resistance, and wider domestic production could make it more widely available.
A production unit at Dushanzi Petrochemical Company in Karamay, Xinjiang, completed a successful trial run on June 27, producing premium-grade rare-earth cis-butadiene rubber. The Chinese Academy of Sciences' Changchun Institute of Applied Chemistry announced the result on July 16.
The institute called the achievement a "major breakthrough" and said the core technologies are "fully under domestic control." It said the project would help meet "urgent demand for high-end grades ," support the petrochemical new-materials industry and help "safeguard supply-chain security."
The process makes two national-standard grades, BR1240 and BR1260, which differ in Mooney viscosity, a standard measure of rubber viscosity and processability. The rubber is made by polymerizing butadiene with a rare-earth catalyst, which helps control the polymer's molecular structure and, in turn, its mechanical properties.
Electric cars tend to be heavier than comparable gasoline vehicles and deliver high torque during acceleration, which places greater demands on tire durability. Low rolling resistance reduces the energy lost as tires deform and roll, while wear and fatigue resistance can extend tire life under repeated stress.
Heavy-duty vehicles also benefit from rubber that can withstand high loads, repeated deformation and heat build-up. Greater resistance to tearing and fatigue can improve durability under demanding conditions.
The institute says the rare-earth version beats conventional nickel-based butadiene rubber on wear resistance, strength, fatigue and tear resistance, low-temperature performance, heat build-up and rolling resistance .
The same properties could matter for military tires and other high-performance rubber parts, though the institute has disclosed nothing about supplying weapons or military vehicles.
The industrial result builds on more than six decades of work at the institute. In 1964, scientists Ouyang Jun and Shen Zhiquan published a paper on rare-earth compounds as catalysts for stereospecific polymerization. The institute describes it as the first international publication on using rare-earth catalysts to produce butadiene rubber.
Work on stereospecific polymerization catalyzed by rare-earth complexes won second prize in China's National Natural Science Award in 1982. Researchers including Bi Jifu, Jiang Liansheng and Zhang Xuequan later ran thousands of scale-up experiments and dozens of pilot trials to develop an industrial process.
A second-generation process led by Bi adds automation and domestically developed technology and equipment. His team tackled precise control of catalyst structure, catalyst preparation, tolerance of different feedstocks, and the integration of long-chain branching and functionalization.
The institute says its work progressed from meeting urgent needs of the national economy to supporting national defense modernization. Earlier defense-related work included liquid polysulfide rubber used as a binder for composite solid propellants, which supported China's "two bombs, one satellite" program.

Apple’s generative AI service, Apple Intelligence, has been registered for use on tablets and laptops in China, Shanghai’s cyberspace regulator announced on Monday. The move expands the service beyond smartphones and follows the company’s earlier regulatory approval for iPhones in July 2026.
China requires companies to register large language models and generative AI services with authorities before offering them to the public. The latest filing adds iPads and Mac laptops as approved uses for the service, clearing a key step toward broader availability across Apple’s device lineup in the mainland market.
Apple has developed a China-specific large language model with support from Alibaba, marking a shift from its approach in other markets. Alibaba’s Qwen model will provide text and image understanding and content generation capabilities through features such as Siri, writing tools, and visual intelligence. Alibaba has stated that these capabilities will be available to Chinese users across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS.
The company has indicated that the features will arrive with the iOS 27.3 update in December 2026, following the release of a test version for developers on November 4. Earlier reporting has also noted involvement by Baidu in certain Apple Intelligence features for Chinese users.
The registration comes nearly two years after Apple Intelligence first launched in other markets, reflecting the time required to meet China’s regulatory standards for AI services. Everyone already knows about the code-in-a-box situation for GTA 6's physical edition on Xbox Series X|S and PS5, but we've also come to learn a few extra details in recent days about what to expect from the boxed copy of the game.
So, when you open up GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S in physical form, you'll be presented with a code that will allow you to redeem the game on the Microsoft Store - essentially converting your physical purchase into a digital one.
Rockstar Games mentioned a shipping date of November 12th for the physical version a few days ago, but we've spotted some retailers saying they'll start shipping on the 11th instead, while a very small number of people even seem to have their copy already.
Once you've got the physical version in your hands, you'll be able to preload GTA 6 in full , although you can technically also do that from tonight by installing the game via the Xbox mobile app.
As you can also see from the tweet above, the physical edition is now confirmed to come with a double-sided A3 poster (at least if you buy from certain retailers). This poster appears to include the game's main artwork along with some character art on the back, so that's at least a nice little bonus to ease the pain of a disc-less release.
But what about a map? Well, Rockstar Games is handling the map a bit differently this time around, making a digital version available to download for free at launch. Alternatively, physical maps will be available to buy from the Rockstar Store "shortly after launch" for $0.99, but we reckon those will be in extreme demand and quickly sell out.
Of course, none of this really changes the fact that the physical edition of GTA 6 is kinda pointless for any platform as things stand, but it does at least make for a good display piece, and it'll be popular for gifting purposes this Christmas.
What's even weirder about this is that Rockstar is supporting GTA 6's launch with various other physical releases, such as an official soundtrack album and all kinds of merch , but it seems there's little hope for a disc version right now.

articles.title_zh: Trump talked with Fed chief, but there’s no record of it on Warsh’s calendar
articles.content_orig:
Tom Boggioni is a writer, born, raised and living in San Diego — where he attended San Diego State University. Prior to writing for Raw Story, he wrote for FireDogLake, blogged as TBogg, and worked in banking, marketing and construction.
Democrats want answers from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh , demanding to know whether he is hiding secret conversations with Donald Trump .
The president says he and Warsh have talked. Warsh’s official records say they haven’t. And the Fed chair isn’t explaining the gap, the Washington Post reported.
On Friday, the Fed released Warsh’s September calendar, and once again, Trump’s name doesn’t appear. That makes "five months in a row," every month since Warsh took over in May, with no logged contact with the president. It comes despite a request this summer from Senate Democrats that he include any such conversations.
According to the Post, " The calendars are one of the few windows into how often a president reaches the official who leads the central bank’s decisions on interest rates , and previous Fed chairs have recorded interactions with presidents there. The Fed is designed to operate independently of the White House , setting rates based on its own best assessment of the economy rather than short-term political pressure."
On Sept. 16, the same day Warsh and his colleagues raised rates a quarter point against Trump’s wishes, the president told reporters he had weighed in on Warsh’s vote.
“I talked to Kevin, and I said, ‘You might as well vote with the board ’cause it’s not gonna matter,’” Trump said, noting that Warsh lacked the votes to change the outcome.
When a reporter asked if he had tried to sway Warsh, Trump said he hadn’t. “No, I didn’t convince him. No, I said, ‘Do what you want,’” he said, adding that he wanted Warsh “to be independent.”
Neither side has cleared it up, the report notes. The White House has refused to say when that conversation took place, and Warsh won’t confirm it ever happened.
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) and three other Democratic senators wrote to Warsh in August, asking him to state in writing whether he had spoken with Trump and to correct his calendars if so. Van Hollen’s office told the Post on Friday that Warsh never replied.
“It’s clear neither Warsh nor Trump give a damn about transparency to the American people,” Van Hollen said. “Under a Democratic majority in Congress, we will continue pushing for that much-needed transparency.”

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals.
Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.
But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says:
Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

articles.title_zh: Syria Signs Deal With China for 6.5 Million Prepaid Electricity Meters, Raising Questions Over Consumer Costs
articles.content_orig:
[DAMASCUS] The Syrian Electricity Company signed an agreement with Chinese company Wasion Group Limited on Sunday to supply 6.5 million prepaid smart electricity meters, as part of efforts to modernize electricity consumption monitoring and improve power grid management in Syria. The deal raises questions about its cost, financing arrangements, and potential impact on consumers’ electricity bills.
The agreement was signed at the Syrian Electricity Company’s headquarters in Damascus, in the presence of representatives from both the Syrian and Chinese sides, as part of a broader government plan to modernize the energy sector and introduce digital systems into electricity services.
The media office of the Syrian Electricity Company, which operates under the Ministry of Energy, told The Media Line that the agreement includes the supply of 6 million single-phase meters, primarily intended for residential properties and small businesses, along with 500,000 three-phase meters, typically used by commercial and industrial facilities requiring greater electrical capacity.
According to the media office, the agreement also includes software systems and technical equipment necessary to operate the meters, allowing for more accurate consumption measurements, improved customer data management, reduced electricity losses, and more efficient network monitoring.
The media office explained that the prepaid metering system requires consumers to purchase electricity credit before using power, rather than paying periodic bills based on consumption recorded after use.
The new system is expected to improve electricity bill collection, reduce errors associated with traditional meter readings, and enable subscribers to monitor their electricity consumption more accurately.

The official announcement did not disclose the financial value of the contract or specify who would bear the costs of purchasing and installing the meters. It also did not clarify whether subscribers would be required to pay fees to replace their existing meters or how the prepaid system would be implemented for low-income households.
Authorities have also not announced a specific timetable for delivering all the meters covered by the agreement or identified which governorates will be included in the initial phase of implementation.
Khaled Abu Di, director of the General Establishment for Electricity Transmission and Distribution, previously announced that the institution had developed a plan to replace conventional electricity meters with smart meters over approximately three years.
In January 2026, Abu Di revealed that around 1.2 million electricity subscribers in Syria still lacked electricity meters, highlighting the scale of the challenges involved in modernizing metering, billing, and revenue collection systems.
The agreement comes as Syria’s electricity sector continues to face significant challenges following years of war, including damage to power generation facilities and transmission and distribution networks, as well as the need for substantial investment to rehabilitate infrastructure and improve the reliability of electricity supplies.
Although introducing smart meters could improve consumption management and reduce commercial electricity losses, modernizing metering systems does not necessarily mean an increase in electricity generation or an end to power outages. Improving the number of hours electricity is available also requires upgrading power plants, transmission and distribution networks, and securing reliable energy supplies.
The prepaid nature of the new meters raises additional questions about their impact on Syrian households, particularly amid difficult economic conditions and concerns about consumers’ ability to regularly purchase electricity credit.
It also remains unclear whether the government intends to introduce changes to electricity tariffs alongside the new system or will limit the initiative to modernizing metering and payment collection procedures.
The agreement represents another step in economic and technological cooperation between Syria and China, as Damascus seeks to attract foreign companies to participate in rehabilitating public services and infrastructure.

Asked about AI executives’ warnings about their models’ safety on 60 Minutes , Trump said, “I think that the risk is not nearly as real as it– as they talk, and I think the risk can be managed, and it’s managed.” He claimed the DOJ is managing that risk, saying, “We had a situation where somebody was reported to us to be doing something bad with AI. We called them very strongly and said, ‘Get ready to go to jail. Please give your wife a kiss good night.’”
Trump refused to name the person or company he was referring to, but said it was the leader of an AI company, “One of the big ones.” He claimed that after the threat of arrest, “this person totally changed everything.” Despite previously claiming that “artificial intelligence” is a term used by people he considers the enemy, Trump said AI rather than SI or super intelligence multiple times during the interview. Eventually he said China’s Xi is “…all in to SI, as I call it, because it really is super intelligence. It’s a much better name, I think, because it’s not artificial.”
60 Minutes ’s Ross Douthat went on to ask if Trump would work with Democrats on AI safety, and Trump said he “absolutely would,” adding, “I don’t mind guardrails, but I don’t want to put us in a deep second position. We’re leading number one. And China has no guardrails, by the way. [...] They have the guardrails that whatever President Xi says goes. With me, it’s pretty strong, but it’s not quite that strong.”

articles.title_orig: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.title_zh: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.content_orig:
Rooftop solar in Chengdu, China. Pexels
China’s carbon dioxide emissions have been flat or falling for more than two years as renewables stunt demand for fossil fuels. But the country just saw its steepest quarterly drop since the Covid pandemic, thanks to energy shocks rippling from the Iran war.
Between July and September, China saw its carbon dioxide emissions fall by 3.1 percent, according to an analysis of official figures and commercial data by Carbon Brief . That is the biggest quarterly decline since the 2022 pandemic lockdowns.
The analysis finds oil use fell by 4 percent, year on year, as Chinese drivers flocked to electric vehicles at a time when the Iran war is driving up the cost of fuel. Electric cars accounted for two in three new passenger vehicles sold in China in September, according to industry data . The uptake of electric cars has helped China ramp down oil imports in the wake of the conflict, analysts find .
Emissions from coal, meanwhile, fell by 3 percent, year on year, as the rapid growth of renewables far outstripped the rise in power demand. China added enough wind, solar, and nuclear generation over the same period to power Germany and more than twice as much as needed to meet China’s growing demand. Emissions from the production of steel and concrete also fell amid the ongoing construction slowdown.
China is continuing to build new coal plants despite the decline in coal generation. As the number of generators grows and the use of coal power declines, the average plant is seeing its running hours drop.
The shift from coal to renewables comes even as large volumes of solar and wind power go unused. China is now generating much more clean electricity than its power grid can handle. In the first six months of this year, China rejected roughly a quarter of its wind and solar output.
Analysts say that China lacks the transmission infrastructure necessary to ferry abundant clean energy from where it is generated to where it is needed. Also at issue is a policy that guarantees the purchase of electricity from newly built coal power plants.

articles.title_orig: Trump Signals Potential Trilateral Talks with China and Russia on Iran War
articles.title_zh: Trump Signals Potential Trilateral Talks with China and Russia on Iran War
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump has indicated the possibility of a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss ending the war with Iran. Concurrently, China’s special envoy on Middle East affairs has traveled to Tehran to meet with officials of the Islamic Republic.
Trump told reporters he expects to meet with his Chinese and Russian counterparts on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China next week. According to Trump, ending the war with Iran and nuclear disarmament are expected to be among the topics of discussion.
The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin was also interested in holding such a summit to discuss peace in Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Zhai Jun, China’s special envoy on Middle East affairs, met with Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, and Majid Takht-Ravanchi, Deputy Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, in Tehran.
This visit comes one week after Ali Bagheri Kani’s trip to Beijing, where he met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The concurrent visit of the Sultan of Oman to China has further fueled speculation regarding potential mediation by Beijing between Tehran and Washington.
China’s Foreign Ministry stated that the objective of these meetings is to review bilateral relations and regional developments in the Middle East.
According to a statement from the ministry, Zhai Jun referenced the widening regional conflict, emphasizing that the use of force is not a solution and that the sovereignty and security of nations must be respected.
The Chinese envoy is scheduled to continue his regional tour with visits to Oman and Saudi Arabia.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese Bag-Maker Songmont Enters Footwear
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese Bag-Maker Songmont Enters Footwear
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Songmont, the Chinese brand that has made global headlines for cultural storytelling that resonates with China ‘s middle class, will launch its first footwear collection Wednesday.
Known for accessories that translate the landscapes, architecture and craft traditions of brand founder Fu Song’s hometown, Shanxi province, the brand is extending its offering beyond bags, ready-to-wear and fragrance with a footwear range inspired by the Wotou shoe.
Wotou is a traditional style named for its resemblance to a dome-shaped steamed corn bun popular in northern China . Traditionally handmade and padded with cotton, the model’s soft construction and distinctive raised seam informed Songmont’s contemporary interpretation for its debut footwear range.
The new silhouette launching this week, retailing for 2,680 renminbi, or $400, echoes the original, while piping joins two leather panels to recreate the ridge across the upper. Songmont’s tiger-tooth hardware adds a modern detail. The toe combines a square shape with softened edges, and layered leather forms a stepped heel inspired by Shanxi architecture. The style will come in 2.5cm and 6cm heel heights.
Songmont said it has spent more than a year developing the shoes, with 20-plus rounds of fittings and refinements. A custom last was designed to accommodate a range of foot shapes, and the use of full-grain cowhide uppers, a double-layer construction, sheepskin lining and high-resilience cotton insoles is meant to balance support, softness and breathability.
The brand added that the footwear launch builds on a design language it has developed across its collections. Its Gather bag, for example, recalls camel bags of the ancient Silk Road, while the Song bucket bag takes cues from traditional kite frameworks.
“As long as we choose things we genuinely like, the brand remains consistent. If we always chase trends or pay too much attention to what’s new, we can end up not knowing what we want,” Fu said about the brand’s approach in an earlier interview with WWD in Paris.
Founded in 2013, Songmont has around 20 stores in China and is expanding at a measured pace, with a focus on customer experience. It plans to open its first Hong Kong store in December, adding a new address as the brand continues to grow beyond mainland China.

articles.title_orig: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.title_zh: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.content_orig:
Fast-food outlets at two prestigious Dolomites resorts are Italy’s first, with legal action threatened
Europe live – latest updates
Skiers on the slopes of two of Italy’s most prestigious resorts will be able to dine from buckets of fried chicken between runs this winter as the US fast-food chain KFC prepares to open outlets, infuriating mountain and food purists while prompting a prominent businessman to threaten legal action.
KFC will open its first high-altitude restaurants on the slopes of Cortina d’Ampezzo and Madonna di Campiglio, in the Dolomites, on 5 December, an initiative the company said was aimed at “surprising people” and “reaching places” where nobody would expect to find it.
The move marks a debut for any fast-food outlet on an Italian ski slope, bringing a menu replete with KFC’s most popular products, from spicy wings and burgers to traditional buckets of fried chicken.
The plans appear to have taken people by surprise, not least Alberico Zardini, a majority shareholder in Faloria Spa, the company that manages the infrastructure on Mount Faloria in Cortina d’Ampezzo, where there is to be a KFC at 2,123 metres.
“The mere idea is disgraceful,” Zardini told Il Messaggero . “It’s absurd and shameful to imagine a fast-food joint in the most beautiful spot in Cortina. Do the people of Cortina not realise what we’re risking here?”
Zardini said he had written to the bosses of Faloria warning that he would pursue legal action unless they put the brakes on KFC’s mountain ambitions.
He said it was “a mad decision”, especially because the outlet would be selling fried chicken inside the Faloria mountain club, where a luxury lodge is due to open on an upper floor. “I am 100% against it and will not just sit back and watch,” he said.
The KFC in Madonna di Campiglio, in south-western Trentino on the opposite side of the Dolomites, will be at 1,700 metres on Piana di Nambino, next door to a swish après-ski club.
The two outlets came under the fast food chain’s “quick service restaurants” product range and were the company’s way of targeting a broader market beyond its loyal Gen Z customers, “from young families to mountain lovers”, said Marzia Farè, the chief marketing officer for KFC Italia.
“We strongly wanted this project because it perfectly represents the way we imagine the evolution of KFC: continuing to surprise, reaching places where no one would expect to find us, and doing so without giving up what makes us unique,” she told brandnews.it .
after newsletter promotion
Needless to say, with the cost of ski passes in Italy increasing each year, the outlets will appeal to those looking for cheap food in otherwise extremely pricey resorts.
But Oscar Farinetti, the founder of Eataly, Italy’s high-end food-store chain, has said the brand “doesn’t belong here at all” – while pointing the blame at customers. “We Italian consumers should be a tad more cultured,” he told Il Sole 24 Ore . “We need to acknowledge our assets – our cuisine made of few ingredients and excellent products. There is a lack of studying one’s own roots – we’re eating fried chicken instead of a nice slice of salami with a glass of fresh wine.”
Luigi Casanova from Mountain Wilderness, an NGO that works to protect mountain environments, told Corriere della Sera : “The era of polenta and luganega sausage is over,” while Paola Demagri, from Trentino’s provincial council, spoke about mountain identity being “sold out to Kentucky chicken”.
Others were more measured in their response. Cristian Ferrari, the president of Società Alpinisti Tridentini, the oldest mountain association in the Trentino area, said: “We have nothing against fried chicken, but are we sure this is the issue we should be most worried about?”

articles.title_orig: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.title_zh: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.content_orig:
Resident birds have returned to Broughshane Waterfowl Park after an oil spill which caused the death of 13 of the flock.
The popular attraction in County Antrim was forced to close after a nearby home heating oil tank was vandalised , causing the oil spill into the pond.
In a post on social media, The Waterfowl Pond confirmed that work is still underway to address the oil contamination and that a number of pens remain out of bounds.
More than 20 birds were transported to the USPCA's headquarters for urgent specialist care following the incident.
The park, which was home to 120 birds, has since reopened.
Broughshane Environment Wildfowl and Wildlife Trust's chairman, Gary Hayward, said about 10-12 birds have returned including two black swans and Nenes.
Hayward said they are back safely in their pens and they are lucky to be healthy.
The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) was first alerted to the incident on Thursday 22 October and have been involved in removing the oil waste.
The agency said the substance involved had been identified as home heating oil or kerosene.
Police said about 44 gallons (200 litres) of oil had leaked from the tank which had been damaged at a business premise in the Main Street area of Broughshane.
Hayward said that there is very little evidence of the oil left as the NIEA have removed the majority of it.
"They have made problems a lot less than they could have been," he told BBC News NI.
He said there is still some oil around the edges, and once the oil leaves the pens the birds will be moved back into them.
The USPCA has also been a key part of the rescue operation.
They said that all of the birds, including geese, ducks and swans, needed bathed and treated due to the level of contamination they suffered.
Unfortunately some had already ingested too much and died as a result.
The Waterfowl Pond offered thanks to the USPCA for looking after the birds.
"We are truly grateful for everything you have done."
It also paid tribute to the support received from the public.
"It's another positive step forward for our park, and we couldn't have got here without you."
Police have said that enquiries into the incident are ongoing and have appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

articles.title_orig: Leaker Envisions a Shorter iPhone With a New iOS Layout
articles.title_zh: Leaker Envisions a Shorter iPhone With a New iOS Layout
articles.content_orig:
A future iPhone could keep its current width while becoming shorter, with iOS preserving room for content by moving some controls into the status bar, in a theory shared by the Weibo leaker known as " Instant Digital ."
Instant Digital imagines Apple shortening a non-folding iPhone once its display has only a single camera cutout or the front-facing camera moves entirely beneath the screen. Taking roughly a status bar's worth of height off the display would bring its aspect ratio from around 19.5:9 to closer to 18:9, apparently making the phone easier to hold and use with one hand.
Controls that currently sit below the status bar could share a row with the time and system indicators. Instant Digital's idea is that combining the two rows would let the shorter display show the same amount of information. The leaker described the layout and proportions as personal speculation.
Apple has already changed how iOS uses the space at the top of the screen with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo . The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌'s smaller Dynamic Island supports up to three simultaneous Live Activities, up from two on earlier models. On the ‌iPhone Duo‌, iOS fits a compact status bar into the corner and positions the Dynamic Island vertically along the side of the outer display.
The timing of a cutout-free display on the iPhone remains uncertain. The leaker "Digital Chat Station" has said Apple is testing under-display camera technology and has described an intermediate design  with a visible hole for the front-facing camera, similar to the ‌iPhone Duo‌.
In a follow-up post on Weibo , another user said they expect iPhones to retain a camera cutout and a 19.5:9 aspect ratio in both 2027 and 2028. Instant Digital replied that some sources say the cutout could disappear in 2028. Display analyst Ross Young has separately said he expects the 2028 iPhone Pro models to retain a centered camera cutout.
In a separate post , Instant Digital said they had a growing hunch that iOS would change substantially after the 20th-anniversary iPhone launches in 2027. They expect changes to how users interact with the software as well as how it looks.
Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman reported that the anniversary iPhone will have curved glass and thinner bezels in the biggest overhaul to the Pro line since the iPhone X. Digital Chat Station has also said Apple was testing a roughly 7-inch display for the largest anniversary model with the same aspect ratio as the iPhone 17 Pro Max.
The iPhone X offers a precedent for a hardware redesign changing how people use iOS. When Apple removed the Home button in 2017, iOS 11 introduced swipe-up navigation on the iPhone X.

articles.title_orig: What Hardware Does Your PC Need To Run A Local AI Model?
articles.title_zh: What Hardware Does Your PC Need To Run A Local AI Model?
articles.content_orig:
I've been a staunch proponent of self-hosting AI for a while now, and the points that I usually make are centered around data privacy and the fiscal cost of self-hosting your own models versus paying for a monthly subscription.
One of the most frequent comments I get says that whatever I save by self-hosting my models is offset by my power bill, which always felt hyperbolic. To find out exactly how much local AI inference adds to my power bill each month, I benchmarked a model with llama-bench, the benchmark tool built into llama.cpp, logged power draw with HWiNFO and Nvidia's own nvidia-smi on my RTX 4070 Ti Super PC, and found that the cost is nowhere close to what I'd pay for a single AI subscription. Here is what I found, and how I measured it.
To make the test and an estimation of cost as comprehensive as possible, I picked Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which is a model that's too big for my RTX 4070 Ti Super's 16GB of GDDR6X memory on its own, and not lacking in capability at any task I throw at it.
At 16.5GB in its UD-IQ4_XS quantization, I tend to offload the experts from eight of its layers to my Ryzen 5 7600X with llama.cpp's --n-cpu-moe flag to get a comfortable inference speed. This also puts the CPU to work on every token generated by the model, so measuring the GPU alone would have concealed a big part of the power bill, which is exactly why I accounted for the CPU in the cost accounting as well.
I used llama-bench , which is a benchmark test that comes baked into llama.cpp (build b11927) to time the two jobs a model does, which is reading prompts and generating tokens. For this test, I gave the model a 2,048 token prompt to read ten times over and instructed it to generate 512 tokens five times over, both starting from an empty context.
While llama-bench ran, I used HWiNFO to log the CPU's package power and nvidia-smi to log the GPU's board power every half a second. Added together, the two peaked at 237.5W while reading and 251.9W while generating.
Then, I took an approach that can be described as hyperbolic in the accounting of costs, which entailed stacking the deck against myself. I priced every token as if my CPU and GPU drew that peak for the entire run, did not subtract their idle draw, and used the U.S. Energy Information Administration's 2026 projected average U.S. residential rate of 18.2 cents per kWh .
The rest of the system, including the RAM, the fans, and power supply losses wasn't logged by HWiNFO, so I'll show what another 100W on top does, which is the figure I would use as the true "worst case."
Cost per million tokens (USD)
To put that in context, or more aptly, in subscription terms, $20 buys about 110 kWh at the currently projected U.S. average rate. At my measured peak of 251.9W, my PC would have to generate tokens non-stop for roughly 436 hours to burn through that, which works out to about 14.5 hours a day, every day, for a month.
Even with the extra 100W on top, it still comes to around 312 hours, or over 10 hours a day. That's counting generation alone, which is the expensive half of the process, since reading a prompt costs well under a cent per million tokens even if you were to consider the worst case.
At this point, you would've likely realized that comparing the cost of running a local model versus paying for a cloud-based subscription service is quite a ridiculous practice. However, there's one final bit of accounting left, and that's comparing the two.
When you pay for a monthly subscription service, the price of each token remains hidden, but the API rate cards from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI don't, which makes them the most fitting standard of measure for what a model's output is worth. I compiled their list prices against my measured numbers for a clear comparison.
Input (per million tokens, USD)
Output (per million tokens, USD)
Output vs Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on RTX 4070 Ti S
67x (Introductory pricing)
There are a lot of misconceptions surrounding the cost of running local models on the hardware you own, particularly relating to power draw. Part of what feeds into these misconceptions is the fact that a GPU running close to its rated power looks and feels energy-intensive, so most people assume that a model keeps the GPU pinned to that figure as long as it's running. However, that is rarely ever the case, because token generation leans on memory more than raw compute.
My RTX 4070 Ti Super peaked at 144W while generating and 177W while reading a prompt against its 285W rating, and even with the CPU's draw and an extra 100W on top, I'd have to keep the model generating continuously for over 10 hours a day before it could match one $20 AI subscription.

articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he was ordering the Justice Department to investigate Democratic leaders over what he described as threats against Republican officials, donors and supporters, without identifying the alleged communications or providing evidence of criminal conduct.
"The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people, including the Attorney General of the United States, and others, with Impeachment and many other forms of punishment, even though they admit they have no reason to do so," Trump said in a Truth Social post .
The alleged threats, the president said, are "extortion at the highest level," he wrote. "I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!"
In his post, Trump claimed that Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan is planning to "go after all young people that believe in Republican Values."
Trump was apparently referencing a speech Slotkin made at a University of Chicago event on Oct. 13. At the time, Slotkin said: "I want young people coming out of school to say, 'Should I go work for the Trump administration?'...I want them to be like, 'Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don't want. And so let me avoid participating in that.' I want that deterrence message sent."
Slotkin alleges that she, her family and her staff faced physical and legal intimidation after the posting of a November 2025 video in which Slotkin and other Democratic leaders called on the U.S. military to "refuse illegal orders" following the airstrikes targeting boats in the Caribbean.
On Nov. 20, Trump called the video treason and said "an example must be set."
The FBI contacted lawmakers, including Slotkin, days later. In February, Slotkin declined to sit for an interview the Justice Department requested about the video.
"The intimidation is the point, and I'm not gonna go along with that," the senator said in February. A federal grand jury later declined to indict the video participants.
Now, Trump alleges Democrats are threatening legal intimidation against Republican leaders and their supporters.
"Republicans should get smart, fast! Threatening letters have been sent to many people, all innocent, from Democrat Political Leaders," the president wrote.
The White House and Slotkin didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
